subject: Archaeology
title: The Copper Age: Metal Begins
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Copper Age: Metal Begins usable.

hook.text: Before bronze, before iron, people figured out that green rocks could be melted into copper — and shaped into tools.

buildup.text: The oldest smelted copper comes from Serbia, dating to about 5000 BCE. It was soft, but it could be resharpened.

discovery.text: Copper axes and ornaments spread through Europe and the Middle East. Metalworking became a specialized craft.

twist.text: Ötzi the Iceman carried a copper axe in 3300 BCE. Chemical analysis traced its copper to Tuscany — 300 miles away.

climax.text: Copper was too soft for heavy work but proved that metals could be extracted from rock. Bronze and iron followed.

punchline.text: Someone melted a green rock and got a knife.

quiz.question: What did Ötzi the Iceman's copper axe reveal?
options: Copper tools were only used by elite warriors
Chemical analysis traced its copper 300 miles to Tuscany, showing long-distance trade
Copper was more durable than bronze for cutting tools
